question: Should OpenClaw add a configuration-enforced concurrency cap per selected subagent target, and should that public setting live under `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent`?
rationale: This is a new compatibility-sensitive config and scheduling policy; source confirms the needed behavior is absent, but maintainers must choose how global, target-agent, parent, and named-lane limits compose.

options.title: Approve target-agent caps
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as an additive per-target limit layered beneath the existing global subagent cap.

options.title: Prefer caller-selected lanes
options.body: Direct users to a separately designed named-lane capability, accepting that it does not automatically constrain all spawns to a given target.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Keep the global cap only until maintainers define a broader concurrency-policy model spanning target, parent, and lane limits.

recommendation.title: Approve target-agent caps
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as an additive per-target limit layered beneath the existing global subagent cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The current global resolver and gateway lane application are the central owner boundary, and prior review history associates this area with steipete.
